items.title: Live: Nifty set for a rebound after 7-day fall; Oil above $92 | Opening Bell
items.description:
Global markets are set for a cautious but positive session as geopolitical tensions around Iran and the Strait of Hormuz remain in focus. Donald Trump warned of “draconian sanctions” against Iran and threatened economic consequences for countries providing support, while the UAE suspended trade with Iran following a ballistic missile attack. Iran, meanwhile, warned Gulf states against assisting US forces, adding to concerns over energy supply and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, where vessel traffic has slowed sharply.
Oil prices strengthened, with Brent crude rising above $92 a barrel. Gold surged 3.4% to $4,479.84 an ounce, hitting a 2.5-month high, while the US dollar recorded its biggest one-day decline in more than three months.
US equities closed higher, with the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq gaining 0.1%-0.2%, although chip stocks weighed on the Nasdaq. Marvell Technology jumped 10% following a chip deal with Alphabet, while Moderna shares surged after encouraging results for its personalised melanoma vaccine.
Bond yields pulled back after the US Treasury announced plans to double government debt repurchases, with the 30-year yield falling 10 bps to 5.1% and the 10-year yield declining 6 bps to 4.6%.
